title: Follow-ups from backend-ibkr-bar-interval-param PR review (#265)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #265 (backend-ibkr-bar-interval-param), which was otherwise accepted.

checklist.step: `_BAR_INTERVAL_STEP['1m']`'s 30-day approximation for IBKR's monthly bar can overshoot the actual bar-to-bar gap whenever a real calendar month is shorter than 30 days (e.g. the Feb->Mar transition in a non-leap year is a 28-day gap). Since the pagination cursor is `earliest - step`, an overshoot produces a `startTime` earlier than the actual preceding bar's timestamp, which (assuming IBKR's documented `startTime` semantics of 'bars at or before this timestamp') would exclude that bar from the next page -- a genuine skip, the same bug class this PR set out to fix for finer intervals, just reintroduced for the coarsest one. Verified by direct simulation (2026-02-01 vs a naive 2026-03-01 minus 30 days = 2026-01-30, which sits before the actual Feb 1 bar). Currently unreachable in practice: `_MAX_BARS_PER_PAGE` (1000) means a monthly-bar page only fills enough to trigger a second page after ~83 years of requested lookback, far beyond any realistic `lookback_days` a caller would pass, so no live code path can hit it today. Worth either using a smaller (never-overshooting) approximation -- e.g. `timedelta(days=27)`, since underestimating the step is safe (only causes redundant/overlapping fetches, deduplicated by the `collected` dict) whereas overestimating it can skip -- or computing the exact prior-month boundary with a calendar-aware step, if/when a caller actually requests `bar_size='1m'`.
